outcome: The einstein problem was already resolved before the frozen revision: David Smith, Joseph Samuel Myers, Craig S. Kaplan and Chaim Goodman-Strauss posted 'An aperiodic monotile' (arXiv:2303.10798) on 20 March 2023, proving the 'hat' polykite (and its mirror) is a single prototile admitting only aperiodic tilings. The same team followed in May 2023 with the 'spectre' tile, which is strictly chiral and aperiodic using only rotations and translations, without needing a mirror image. Both predate the 26 January 2024 snapshot. The only things that happened inside the window are the formal journal publication of the hat paper (Combinatorial Theory, July 2024) and an unrelated physical/chemical analogue (Empa, February 2025).
summary: This problem was resolved before the frozen revision's date, not during the measurement window. Smith discovered the 'hat' shape in November 2022; the team of Smith, Myers, Kaplan and Goodman-Strauss posted the proof that it (with its mirror image) is an aperiodic monotile as arXiv:2303.10798 on 20 March 2023, using a combinatorial argument with a computer-assisted (exhaustive/combinatorial search, not AI/ML) verification of the substitution/hierarchical tiling structure. In May 2023 the same group found the 'spectre' tile, a strictly chiral aperiodic monotile requiring no reflections at all (arXiv:2306.06512 and related work), an even stronger case of the same problem, also pre-window. Both fully answer the einstein problem as stated ('does there exist a shape that is a prototile for an aperiodic tiling but not for any periodic tiling') in the affirmative, well before 26 January 2024. Inside the window itself, the only things that happened are: (1) the hat paper's formal peer-reviewed publication in Combinatorial Theory in July 2024 — this is the same 2023 result reaching journal form, not a new mathematical event, so per §6.3 it is not what the date is set to; and (2) a February 2025 Empa physics/chemistry result showing a chiral molecule forms aperiodic (non-repeating) patterns on a silver surface — this is a physical analogue/related phenomenon in a different domain (surface science), not a case or extension of the stated geometric tiling problem, so per §3.1 it does not count as a change to this problem. I found no trace of any AI system (LLM, ML model, or AI-branded tool) involved in either the hat/spectre discovery/proof or in the 2025 Empa work; 'computer-assisted proof' in the hat paper refers to a finite combinatorial case-check of substitution rules, which is not an AI system under §6.2. I agree with the triage's verdict and reasoning.
competing_reading: One could argue the spectre tile (May 2023) is itself a distinct, stronger case worth dating as a second pre-window event, but since both are pre-window this does not change the status. One could also argue the July 2024 journal publication should be treated as the 'event' since it falls inside the window, but §6.3 explicitly says to date by the first written argument (the March 2023 preprint), not the journal publication, precisely to avoid this kind of window-shifting.
what_would_settle_it: Nothing further is needed to settle the classification; it would only change if a still-earlier, non-aperiodic monotile claim were found to predate Smith's 2022 discovery, which is not the case.
